places.name: Amsterdam
places.summary: The Dutch capital, built around a 17th-century ring of canals lined with gabled merchants' houses, with world-class museums and a lively café and bar scene. Compact and best explored on foot, by bike or by boat.
facts: Don't drive in: city-centre parking costs ~€7.50 an hour; use a P+R (from ~€1–6 a day with public-transport use)
Museumkaart (~€75 a year) gives free entry to most Dutch museums and pays off after 4–5 visits
Watch out for cyclists: never walk in the red bike lanes
Trains from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal take about 15 minutes

places.name: Rijksmuseum
places.summary: The national museum of the Netherlands, with Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's Milkmaid and a huge collection of Golden Age painting, ship models and Delftware. One of the great museums of Europe.
facts: ~€25 adult; free with Museumkaart, under-18s free
Book a timed entry slot online (also needed with a Museumkaart)
Go at opening or after 15:00 to avoid the busiest hours
The underpass through the building is a public cycle path and free to walk

places.name: Van Gogh Museum
places.summary: The world's largest collection of Van Gogh's paintings and drawings, hung chronologically so you can follow his development from dark Brabant peasant scenes to the Sunflowers and the late Auvers works.
facts: ~€22 adult; free with Museumkaart but a timed slot must still be booked
Tickets are sold online only, for a fixed time slot — book days or weeks ahead in summer
Allow about 2 hours; the audio guide is worthwhile
On Museumplein next to the Rijksmuseum and Stedelijk

places.name: Anne Frank House
places.summary: The canal-side house where Anne Frank and her family hid from the Nazis for two years, including the secret annexe behind the bookcase. A moving, carefully presented museum about the diary and the Holocaust.
facts: ~€16 adult; NOT included in the Museumkaart
Tickets are sold online only for a timed slot, released about 6 weeks ahead — they sell out fast
Steep stairs, not suitable for wheelchairs in the annexe
Allow about 1–1.5 hours

places.name: Amsterdam canal cruise
places.summary: A boat trip through the UNESCO-listed canal ring is the best way to grasp how the city was built, gliding past gabled houses, bridges and houseboats. Departures from Centraal Station, Damrak and the Rijksmuseum.
facts: Large glass-topped boats ~€18–20 for an hour; smaller open boats cost more but are nicer
Evening cruises are lovely when the bridges are lit
Book ahead in summer or pick a small-boat operator

places.name: Jordaan
places.summary: Former working-class quarter west of the canal ring, now a maze of narrow streets, small canals, hidden courtyard almshouses (hofjes), brown cafés and independent shops. Best for wandering.
facts: Free; best on foot
Monday morning Noordermarkt flea market and Saturday organic market
Combine with the Nine Streets (Negen Straatjes) shopping area

places.name: Royal Palace Amsterdam (Paleis op de Dam)
places.summary: Built as the city hall in the 17th century at the height of the Dutch Golden Age, with a vast marble Citizens' Hall. Still used by the King for state occasions.
facts: ~€12–15 adult; free with Museumkaart, free audio guide
Closes for royal events — check the calendar before going
Right on Dam Square

places.name: Stedelijk Museum
places.summary: The Netherlands' leading museum of modern and contemporary art and design: Mondrian, Malevich, De Stijl, Appel and Warhol, in a building nicknamed 'the bathtub'.
facts: ~€22 adult; free with Museumkaart
On Museumplein, quieter than its neighbours
Allow about 2 hours

places.name: Rembrandt House Museum
places.summary: The house where Rembrandt lived and worked from 1639 to 1658, furnished as in his day, with his studio, etchings and printing demonstrations.
facts: ~€18 adult; free with Museumkaart
Booking a time slot online is recommended
Next to the Waterlooplein flea market

places.name: Our Lord in the Attic (Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder)
places.summary: A complete 17th-century canal house with a secret Catholic church hidden in its attic, from the time when Catholic worship was banned in public. A small, atmospheric surprise in the old centre.
facts: ~€17 adult; free with Museumkaart
Steep stairs
On the edge of the Red Light District, near Centraal Station

places.name: Begijnhof
places.summary: A quiet medieval courtyard of almshouses around a lawn, founded for the Beguines, with Amsterdam's oldest wooden house (Het Houten Huis) and a hidden church.
facts: Free
Residents live here: keep quiet, no groups; closed in the evening
Entrance via a small gate off the Spui

places.name: Vondelpark
places.summary: Amsterdam's favourite park, a 19th-century landscape of ponds, lawns and an open-air theatre, busy with cyclists, joggers and picnickers on sunny days.
facts: Free, open around the clock
Ideal break between the Museumplein museums
Free open-air theatre in summer

places.name: Albert Cuyp Market
places.summary: The city's largest street market in the multicultural De Pijp district, with stalls of cheese, herring, fruit and fabrics, and fresh stroopwafels made to order.
facts: Free; roughly 09:00–17:00 Monday to Saturday
Try raw herring, kibbeling and a warm stroopwafel
Surrounded by good cafés and restaurants

places.name: A'DAM Lookout
places.summary: Observation deck on top of the A'DAM Tower in Amsterdam-Noord, with a 360° view over the city, harbour and IJ, and a swing over the edge.
facts: ~€17 adult, more with the 'Over the Edge' swing
Free ferry from behind Centraal Station takes 3 minutes
Good at sunset

places.name: Haarlem
places.summary: Handsome historic city around the Grote Markt and the huge St Bavo church, with canals, almshouse courtyards and excellent museums. A relaxed alternative base 15 minutes by train from Amsterdam.
facts: Trains to Amsterdam Centraal every few minutes (~15 minutes)
Park in a garage or P+R; centre streets are mostly car-free
Saturday market on the Grote Markt
Close to the beaches at Zandvoort and Bloemendaal

places.name: Frans Hals Museum
places.summary: Golden Age portraits by Frans Hals displayed in a 17th-century old men's almshouse around a courtyard garden. Intimate and much quieter than the Amsterdam museums.
facts: ~€18 adult; free with Museumkaart
Allow 1–1.5 hours
Short walk south of the Grote Markt

places.name: Teylers Museum
places.summary: The oldest museum in the Netherlands (1784), a perfectly preserved cabinet of fossils, scientific instruments and drawings by Michelangelo and Rembrandt in period display cases.
facts: ~€17 adult; free with Museumkaart
The Oval Room is the highlight
On the Spaarne river

places.name: Zaanse Schans
places.summary: Riverside open-air collection of working windmills, green wooden houses, a clog workshop and cheese farm on the Zaan. Touristy but the easiest place near Amsterdam to step inside working mills.
facts: Free to enter the area; mills and museums charge ~€5–8 each (Zaans Museum free with Museumkaart)
Paid car park; or take the train to Zaandijk Zaanse Schans and walk 15 minutes
Very busy with tour coaches from mid-morning: arrive early or late afternoon
Mills open mainly April–October

places.name: Alkmaar
places.summary: Lively canal town best known for its traditional cheese market, with a well-kept old centre, the Grote Kerk and the Waag weigh house. A good base for the north and the ferry to Texel.
facts: About 35–40 minutes by train from Amsterdam
Park in a garage at the edge of the centre
Base for Texel: drive or take bus/train to Den Helder for the ferry

places.name: Alkmaar Cheese Market
places.summary: A centuries-old cheese market re-enacted on the Waagplein: cheese carriers in white with coloured straw hats trot wheels of Gouda on wooden barrows to the weigh house.
facts: Free; Fridays 10:00–12:30 from late March to late September only
Arrive by 09:30 for a front-row spot by the ropes
Cheese stalls and the Dutch Cheese Museum in the Waag
places.season: Only held on Fridays from late March to late September.

places.name: Volendam
places.summary: Former fishing village on the IJsselmeer with a busy harbour-front promenade, souvenir shops and smoked-eel stalls. Very touristy, but the boat to Marken makes a nice combination.
facts: Free; paid parking at the edge of the village
Try smoked eel or kibbeling on the dyke
Marken Express boat to Marken every 30–45 minutes (~30 minutes, spring–autumn)

places.name: Edam
places.summary: Small, quiet canal town that gave its name to the cheese, with lifting bridges, a cheese weigh house and a summer cheese market. Far calmer than nearby Volendam.
facts: Free; park at the edge of town
Cheese market on Wednesday mornings in July and August
Easy to cycle from Volendam (3 km)

places.name: Marken
places.summary: Former island of wooden houses on mounds, painted green and black, joined to the mainland by a causeway. A walk out to the little Paard van Marken lighthouse is a highlight.
facts: Free; car park at the village entrance (cars not allowed in)
Combine with Volendam by the Marken Express boat
Walk to the lighthouse takes about 45 minutes each way

places.name: Hoorn
places.summary: Prosperous former VOC port on the IJsselmeer with a picturesque harbour, the Hoofdtoren tower and a Golden Age centre. Starting point of the steam tram to Medemblik.
facts: About 35–40 minutes by train from Amsterdam
Steam tram Hoorn–Medemblik runs April–October (combined with a boat back)
Westfries Museum on the Roode Steen square (Museumkaart)

places.name: Zuiderzee Museum, Enkhuizen
places.summary: Large open-air museum of relocated houses, shops and workshops from the old Zuiderzee fishing towns, with craftspeople at work and an indoor museum of boats.
facts: ~€20 adult; free with Museumkaart
The open-air part is open roughly April–October only
Enkhuizen old town and harbours are worth a stroll too
Allow at least half a day
places.season: The open-air museum is only open from spring to autumn.

places.name: Muiderslot
places.summary: Moated brick castle from the 13th century at the mouth of the Vecht, the best-preserved medieval castle in the Netherlands, with furnished rooms and a herb garden.
facts: ~€18 adult; free with Museumkaart
20 minutes' drive from Amsterdam
Children's activities and falconry in summer

places.name: Naarden Vesting
places.summary: Small town inside a near-perfect star-shaped fortress of double moats and bastions, with a fortress museum in the casemates. Best walked or seen by boat around the walls.
facts: Free to walk the ramparts; Vestingmuseum free with Museumkaart
Boat trips around the moats in summer
About 25 minutes from Amsterdam

places.name: Texel (Den Burg)
places.summary: The largest Wadden island, an easy ferry hop from Den Helder, with long sandy beaches, dunes, sheep, bird reserves and cycling paths. Den Burg is the main village.
facts: TESO ferry Den Helder–'t Horntje every hour, 20 minutes; pay for the return only (~€3 foot passenger, ~€40 car)
Bring or hire bikes: the island is made for cycling
Book accommodation ahead in summer

places.name: Dunes of Texel National Park & Ecomare
places.summary: Dunes, heath and salt marshes along Texel's west coast, including the tidal inlet of De Slufter. Ecomare at De Koog combines a seal sanctuary with a nature museum.
facts: Ecomare ~€18 adult
Seal feeding at Ecomare at fixed times
Good cycling and walking trails; stay on paths in the breeding season

places.name: Zandvoort beach
places.summary: The closest seaside resort to Amsterdam, with a long, wide sandy beach lined with beach pavilions. Crowded on hot summer weekends.
facts: Direct trains from Amsterdam via Haarlem (~30 minutes)
Parking is expensive and fills up on sunny days — take the train
Quieter beaches north at Bloemendaal
places.season: Sea water is cold; swimmable only in July–August for most.

places.name: Zuid-Kennemerland National Park
places.summary: Coastal dunes, woods and lakes between Haarlem and the sea, home to free-roaming wisent (European bison), Scottish Highland cattle and fallow deer.
facts: Free; paid parking at the entrances
Visitor centre De Zandwaaier at Bloemendaal
Good walking and cycling loops to the beach

places.name: Leiden
places.summary: University city on canals, Rembrandt's birthplace, with an excellent set of museums, almshouse courtyards and windmills. A good-value base between Amsterdam, Keukenhof and The Hague.
facts: About 35 minutes by train from Amsterdam, 15 from Schiphol
Park in a garage or P+R; the centre is walkable
Saturday market along the Nieuwe Rijn
Closest town to Keukenhof (bus from Leiden Centraal in season)

places.name: National Museum of Antiquities (RMO)
places.summary: The Dutch national archaeology museum, with a real Egyptian temple (Taffeh) in its hall, mummies and Greek, Roman and early Dutch collections.
facts: ~€17 adult; free with Museumkaart
Good for children
Central Leiden on the Rapenburg

places.name: Keukenhof
places.summary: The world's best-known spring flower garden: about seven million tulips, daffodils and hyacinths planted each year in 32 hectares of landscaped park, surrounded by the bulb fields.
facts: Open only about 8 weeks, mid-March to mid-May; ~€20 adult, NOT in the Museumkaart
Buy dated online tickets in advance; also book a time slot for parking (~€8)
Arrive at opening or after 16:00 to avoid the crowds
Express bus from Schiphol and Leiden in season
places.season: Tulips usually peak mid to late April; open only from mid-March to mid-May.

places.name: Bulb fields bike ride (Bollenstreek)
places.summary: Cycling the flat country lanes between Lisse, Hillegom and Noordwijkerhout through striped fields of tulips and hyacinths in bloom. Bikes can be hired opposite Keukenhof.
facts: Bike hire ~€15–20 a day
Fields are private: look from the road, don't walk into them
Signposted routes with numbered junctions (knooppunten)
places.season: Fields bloom from late March (daffodils, hyacinths) to early May (tulips); the flowers are cut soon after.

places.name: The Hague (Den Haag)
places.summary: Seat of the Dutch government and royal family, an elegant city of embassies, palaces and fine museums, with the beach at Scheveningen 15 minutes away by tram.
facts: The Binnenhof parliament complex is under renovation until around 2028
Park in a P+R or garage; trams cover the city
The Hague Centraal and Hollands Spoor stations both have intercity trains

places.name: Mauritshuis
places.summary: A small 17th-century palace holding a superb collection of Dutch Golden Age art, including Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring and View of Delft and Rembrandt's Anatomy Lesson.
facts: ~€18 adult; free with Museumkaart
Booking a time slot online is recommended
Allow 1.5 hours; compact and easy to see

places.name: Scheveningen
places.summary: The Hague's seaside district, with a long sandy beach, the grand Kurhaus hotel, a pier with a Ferris wheel and a fishing harbour with good fish restaurants.
facts: Tram 1 or 9 from the centre (~20 minutes)
Paid parking; garages fill on sunny weekends
Harbour side is quieter and better for food

places.name: Madurodam
places.summary: Miniature park showing the Netherlands' famous buildings, canals, ports and Schiphol at 1:25 scale, with interactive models. Popular with families.
facts: Book online for a discount
Allow about 2 hours
Between the centre and Scheveningen

places.name: Delft
places.summary: Picture-perfect canal town of Vermeer and Delft Blue pottery, with a grand Markt between the Nieuwe Kerk and the town hall. Small, walkable and lovely in the evening.
facts: 10–15 minutes by train from The Hague or Rotterdam
Park in a garage at the edge; the centre is largely car-free
Thursday market on the Markt
Royal Delft pottery factory tours south of the centre

places.name: Nieuwe Kerk, Delft
places.summary: Gothic church on the Markt holding the mausoleum of William of Orange and the royal family's burial vault. Climb the 376 steps of the tower for a view to The Hague and Rotterdam.
facts: Combined ticket with the Oude Kerk; tower climb extra
Tower climb is narrow and steep
Allow about 1 hour

places.name: Rotterdam
places.summary: Europe's largest port city, rebuilt after 1940 as a showcase of bold modern architecture, with a lively food scene, the Erasmus Bridge and the Maas river. Feels nothing like the canal towns.
facts: Park in a P+R and use the metro; city garages are expensive
Water taxis and waterbuses cross the Maas
~40 minutes by intercity from Amsterdam

places.name: Markthal
places.summary: A giant horseshoe of apartments arching over a covered food hall, its ceiling painted with a huge fruit-and-vegetable mural. Good for a quick lunch.
facts: Free
Outdoor Blaak market on Tuesdays and Saturdays next door
Cube Houses are across the road

places.name: Cube Houses (Kubuswoningen)
places.summary: Piet Blom's 1984 tilted yellow cube houses on poles above a street near the Old Harbour. One show cube is open to visitors.
facts: Show cube ~€3–4
Next to the Markthal and the Old Harbour
15–30 minutes is enough

places.name: Euromast
places.summary: 185 m observation tower beside the Park, with a viewing deck and a rotating glass lift to the top giving views over the port and skyline.
facts: Adult ticket ~€19
Choose a clear day
Walkable from Delfshaven

places.name: Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen
places.summary: The world's first publicly accessible art storage building, a mirrored bowl in the Museumpark where you can wander among stored masterpieces and restorers at work, with a rooftop birch forest.
facts: Book a time slot online
The rooftop restaurant and terrace give a good city view
Allow about 1.5 hours

places.name: Delfshaven
places.summary: The only part of old Rotterdam to survive the 1940 bombing: a small harbour with old warehouses, a windmill and the church where the Pilgrim Fathers prayed before sailing to America.
facts: Free
Metro or tram from the centre
Good brown cafés and a craft brewery on the harbour

places.name: Kinderdijk
places.summary: UNESCO-listed line of 19 18th-century windmills along the polder canals, built to drain the land. The most iconic windmill landscape in the country; two mills can be visited inside.
facts: ~€19 adult for the mill interiors, film and boat; walking or cycling the path along the mills is free
Waterbus from Rotterdam (Erasmusbrug) is the nicest way to come
Paid car park; arrive early to beat the coach groups
Mills turn on Saturdays in season

places.name: Gouda
places.summary: Small canal town with a Gothic town hall standing alone on a triangular market square, the long St John's church with famous 16th-century stained glass, and of course cheese.
facts: Traditional cheese market Thursday mornings (about 10:00–12:30), April to August
St Janskerk ~€10, worth it for the windows
Fresh stroopwafels were invented here

places.name: Dordrecht
places.summary: The oldest city in Holland, on a river junction, with old harbours, merchant houses and the massive Grote Kerk tower. Gateway to the Biesbosch.
facts: Waterbus to Rotterdam and Kinderdijk
Climb the Grote Kerk tower for river views
Dordrechts Museum free with Museumkaart

places.name: Utrecht
places.summary: Lively university city with a medieval centre around the Dom tower, and unique two-level canals whose old wharf cellars are now cafés at water level. Less touristy than Amsterdam and very central.
facts: ~25 minutes by train from Amsterdam; Utrecht Centraal is the country's rail hub
Park at P+R Papendorp or Westraven and take the tram
Hire a canal boat or pedal boat on the Oudegracht

places.name: Dom Tower
places.summary: At 112 m the tallest church tower in the Netherlands, climbed by 465 steps with a guide. On a clear day you can see Amsterdam.
facts: ~€12 adult; guided tours only, book online in advance
Not for those with vertigo or knee problems
Underground DOMunder tour shows the Roman fort foundations

places.name: Oudegracht wharves
places.summary: Utrecht's main canal with its medieval wharves and cellars right at the waterline, now terraces and restaurants. Unlike any other Dutch canal.
facts: Free
Canal cruises leave from the Oudegracht (~1 hour)
Lovely on summer evenings

places.name: Rietveld Schröder House
places.summary: UNESCO-listed 1924 house by Gerrit Rietveld, the purest built expression of De Stijl with movable walls and primary colours. Small and visited by guided tour.
facts: Book ahead via the Centraal Museum; small groups only
Free with Museumkaart (booking still required)
Bus or 20-minute walk from the centre

places.name: Railway Museum (Spoorwegmuseum)
places.summary: National railway museum in an old station, with historic locomotives and themed rides. A strong choice with children.
facts: Book online
Allow 2–3 hours
Short walk or shuttle train from Utrecht Centraal

places.name: Castle De Haar
places.summary: The largest castle in the Netherlands, a fairy-tale neo-Gothic rebuild (1892) of a medieval ruin, with lavish interiors and extensive formal gardens and moats.
facts: Book online; castle interior and gardens ticket ~€20
Free car park
20 minutes' drive from Utrecht; the gardens alone are worth a visit

places.name: Amersfoort
places.summary: Medieval town with a ring of canals, the Koppelpoort water gate and the tall Onze Lieve Vrouwetoren. Lively but rarely crowded, and the birthplace of Mondrian.
facts: 15 minutes by train from Utrecht
Park in a garage near the old town
Mondriaanhuis free with Museumkaart

places.name: Amerongen Castle
places.summary: Moated 17th-century country house where the German Kaiser Wilhelm II stayed after fleeing in 1918, with original interiors and gardens.
facts: Free with Museumkaart
Allow about 1.5 hours with the gardens
Combine with the Utrechtse Heuvelrug and Wijk bij Duurstede

places.name: Utrechtse Heuvelrug National Park
places.summary: A glacial ridge of forest and heath east of Utrecht, with walking and cycling trails and views over the Rhine valley from the Amerongse Berg.
facts: Free
Many marked walks of 5–10 km
Heather blooms in August

places.name: Wijk bij Duurstede
places.summary: Small fortified town on the Lek, once the Viking-era trading town of Dorestad, with a castle park and the windmill Rijn en Lek painted by Jacob van Ruisdael.
facts: Free
Pleasant cycling along the river dykes
Quiet, few tourists

places.name: Fort Vechten – Waterline Museum
places.summary: The largest fort of the UNESCO-listed Dutch Water Line, with a museum explaining how the land was flooded to stop invaders.
facts: Free with Museumkaart
Easy by bike from Utrecht (~25 minutes)
Combine with a ride along the forts

places.name: Loosdrecht Lakes
places.summary: Lakes formed by peat digging along the Vecht river, with sailing, rental boats and cycling between villages and country houses.
facts: Rent an electric boat for a few hours
Cycle the Vecht valley with its country estates
Busy on summer weekends

places.name: Middelburg
places.summary: Capital of Zeeland, a prosperous medieval trading town rebuilt after 1940, with a large abbey complex, a fine Gothic town hall and quiet streets of merchant houses. The best base for Walcheren.
facts: About 2.5 hours by train from Amsterdam
Park in a garage or at the edge; the centre is compact
Thursday market on the Markt
Close to the beaches at Domburg and Zoutelande

places.name: Middelburg Abbey & Lange Jan
places.summary: Medieval abbey complex housing the provincial government, the Zeeuws Museum with its Zeeland tapestries, and the 91 m Lange Jan tower.
facts: Zeeuws Museum free with Museumkaart
Climb the Lange Jan for views over Walcheren (in season)
Abbey courtyard free

places.name: Veere
places.summary: Tiny former port that once held the Scottish wool trade monopoly, with a huge unfinished church, a Gothic town hall and a yacht harbour on the Veerse Meer.
facts: Free; park at the edge of the village
Lovely cycle from Middelburg (~7 km)
Quiet in the evening once day-trippers leave

places.name: Zierikzee
places.summary: Well-preserved old harbour town on Schouwen-Duiveland with harbour gates, the tall unfinished St Lievens tower and narrow streets. Departure point for seal-watching trips on the Oosterschelde.
facts: Park outside the ring canal
Thursday market
Base for Neeltje Jans and the Watersnoodmuseum

places.name: Delta Works: Oosterscheldekering & Neeltje Jans
places.summary: The largest of the Delta Works, a 9 km storm-surge barrier with giant sliding gates built after the 1953 flood. The Deltapark Neeltje Jans on the artificial island explains it and lets you walk inside a pier.
facts: Deltapark ~€27 adult with exhibitions, seal show and boat trip
Driving across the barrier is free
Allow half a day for the park

places.name: Watersnoodmuseum
places.summary: Moving museum about the 1953 North Sea flood that killed 1,836 people, set inside four concrete caissons used to close the last dike breach at Ouwerkerk.
facts: Free with Museumkaart
Allow about 2 hours
Free parking

places.name: Domburg
places.summary: Zeeland's oldest seaside resort, with a broad sandy beach backed by high dunes and an elegant small-town centre that drew artists such as Mondrian.
facts: Paid parking behind the dunes
Wooded dune walks towards Oostkapelle
Good base for a beach stay
places.season: Busiest in July–August; spring and September are calmer.

places.name: Zoutelande
places.summary: Small resort on the south-west coast of Walcheren, the only Dutch North Sea beach facing south-west, with sunny afternoons and big ships passing to Antwerp.
facts: Paid parking
Walk the dyke to Westkapelle
Swimming in summer only

places.name: Westkapelle Lighthouse (Westkapelle Hoog)
places.summary: A lighthouse built on top of the tower of a medieval church, standing in the middle of the village behind the sea dyke. Climb it for a view over Walcheren.
facts: Small entry fee to climb, in season
Polderhuis museum on the 1944 inundation nearby
Combine with the Westkapelle sea dyke

places.name: Vlissingen
places.summary: Port town at the mouth of the Westerschelde, with a seafront boulevard where huge container ships pass close by, and a pedestrian ferry to Breskens.
facts: Watch ships from the Boulevard de Ruyter
Fast foot ferry to Breskens in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen
Muzeeum (maritime) free with Museumkaart

places.name: Oosterschelde seal-spotting boat trip
places.summary: Boat trips from Zierikzee into the Oosterschelde National Park, the largest Dutch national park, to see harbour and grey seals hauled out on sandbanks.
facts: Book ahead; trips depend on the tide
Bring binoculars and warm layers
Spring to autumn

places.name: Renesse
places.summary: Popular resort on Schouwen-Duiveland with one of the widest beaches in the country and dunes behind; the Brouwersdam nearby is a kitesurf hotspot.
facts: Paid parking
Busy with young holidaymakers in summer
Moriaanshoofd beach is quieter

places.name: Yerseke
places.summary: The mussel and oyster capital of the Netherlands, with oyster pits along the Oosterschelde and seafood restaurants on the harbour.
facts: Mussel season runs roughly July to April
Oyster tasting at the pits by the dyke
Day trip from Middelburg or Zierikzee

places.name: Sluis
places.summary: Tiny fortified town in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen near the Belgian border, with the only belfry in the Netherlands and a windmill on the ramparts. Close to Bruges.
facts: Free
Busy with Belgian shoppers on weekends
Reach via the Westerschelde tunnel (toll ~€5)
